title: Snow, and the Others
subtitle: We're not even halfway through this journey, but we will press on.

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: I've always believed it! We can dig through the frozen layers and find ways to survive here. Even when the harsh northern winds gnash their teeth, we can overcome any challenge!

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: Zeno will have its own specific guidelines that I doubt I'll be able to adapt to, but just like this particular component, we are already refined and capable enough!

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: Yes, we can live on our own without relying on other leaders.

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: Let me be honest, I am not much of a fighter. The only tools I know how to use are a wrench and pliers. But when push comes to shove, I will make do with whatever I can get my hands on. We need weapons to defend ourselves, and we are not afraid to use them.

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: It is crucial for children to explore the world. I came here at a young age, on a whim with a friend. We had no experience in shaping workpieces or handling raw materials. Now, my skills are highly valued in this community.

content.speaker: Elena
content.text: We did not come to Rayashki to have fun. They've got it all wrong.

trails.title: No Man's Land
trails.description: After people leave, new inhabitants arrive. However, they don't seem to be very interested in socializing.

items.text: New Mine, Rayashki
The unsupported ley energy returns to the earth.
The soil is smoothed out, a canvas for a new painting.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Take heart, comrades.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Everything he did was for Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We shared the same dream, didn't we?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: To do all we can for the good of the people.
She faces toward the silent cliffs.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Reporting: drilling rig clear, ready for new exploration.
He stomps firmly on the ground beneath his feet.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: That's the spirit! We must keep going! Let's get some wiggles!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Yuri, start the machines!

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: On it!
A loud call resounds, and the huge drill churns once more.
The steel behemoths roar.
Their sound covering up the sorrow and the gloom of the moment.
After some time, the children carefully and cautiously approach the cliff's edge.
Avgust bends down, placing his sunflower on the edge, as tenderly as a mother tucks in their child.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Take this. It's my best friend.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I think it will be glad to have another best friend.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: I will become a great hero like you. It's a promise, a man's promise.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Why are your feathers wet, Pyotr?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: You have water on your face, Ms. Windsong. Can kids still cry after they grow up?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I should've known ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The abnormal fluctuation of the ley energy, and how much of an attraction it is to the critters ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I should've noticed they were different from my theory.
Her words are met by murmurs, but a familiar hand wraps hers gently.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: At least this experience will be valuable for the study of ley lines, won't it?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Take it in, and make something of it. I'm sure it will be of more help in the future.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You're not only doing this for yourself or for me, but for those who sacrificed for all of us.
*boom*

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: We found it! This must be the new resource!
A stream of black rocks rises from the pile, one by one.
In a short time, they are picked up and passed through countless hands.
The air is thick with black dust that covers coats, gloves, boots, and faces.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: COAL!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: It is coal! We did it!

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: This is our coal! Comrades, we will use it to cook our meal tonight!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: And it will be the best meal I've ever had!

items.speaker: Patrik
items.text: Is that so, Comrade Nikita? You got a problem with my food, huh?

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Hahahaha!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: I made a rough estimate. The reserves here should last hundreds of years!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: For the first time in history, the theory of ley lines has been verified.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There is no doubt your work deserves a fair assessment now.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thank you for your help, Ms. Vila.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We achieved this together, didn't we?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Of course.
Cheers travel forward and back over the crowd and out into the boundless tundra.
They echo against the cliffs.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The glory goes to every one of us.
Their joy reaches back to the town, carried in by the victorious comrades-in-arms.
Unfortunately, their now-unwelcome guests seem unable to share in the enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I'm very glad to see you again, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hmph! Are you? You don't look glad at all.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Heh. I admit, I underestimated the people here.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Especially you, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The great heroine who found coal deep beneath the town.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So, did I manage to ruin Zeno's little plans?
Her sharp tongue breaks the cool of the no longer smiling crocodile.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We have nothing left to do here. Zeno will leave soon.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I know we disagree on many things, our future included. Still, Zeno looks forward to working with you again, hopefully in a more friendly way.
He extends his hand on his own initiative.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I hope so, too.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You don't wanna be embarrassed by another lowly researcher again, do you?
Bertolt's hand awkwardly hangs in the air, unanswered.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Goodbye, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Wait! I have one last question!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Please, I'm at your service.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Zeno confirmed the existence of Hoituks in Rayashki months ago, but you just took care of them without letting anyone know.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You already knew there would be a large reserve of coal here, didn't you?!
He shrugs and leaves without another word.
